pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values - Maple Walk School
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our core values:
Curiosity to seek knowledge and love learning
Creativity to innovate and collaborate
Community to foster a sense of belonging
Our Vision:
To provide an excellent, forward-thinking education that inspires and challenges every child
To recognise the value of knowledge and how it helps children to understand their world and the positive difference they can make
To instil a love of learning through a broad, exciting curriculum with strong foundations in literacy and numeracy
To empower pupils with a sense of belonging, allowing them to fulfil their potential and grow in confidence
To value the diversity of our community by celebrating all religions, beliefs, backgrounds and cultures
To offer a great value education, enabling as many families as possible to benefit from our ‘not-for-profit’ ethos
Our Approach
We believe that learning should be rich, varied and exciting. It should be taught creatively and individually tailored.
The New Model School Company (NMS) offers a great value education. We are forward thinking – sustainability is central to our ethos and our school buildings are modern and innovative. We deliver an ambitious knowledge-based curriculum that is taught in a creative way. We are confident that what we teach, and how we teach it, is truly excellent.
By embedding our pupils learning in the community and using the best of what the neighbourhood has to offer, whether that be Roundwood Park or the River Thames, we provide our pupils with a deeper learning experience.
From Year 1, NMS pupils are taught content-rich subjects rooted in the arts and sciences. We believe that it is through acquiring knowledge that a child is inspired to become a lifelong learner. This emphasis also provides our children with the solid foundations to grasp a wider range of subjects later in their formal education.
Creativity and curiosity are two of our key values. Our pupils are given the opportunity to take part in many different sports and a wide range of arts such as Music, Drama and Dance, all taught by specialist teachers.
Regular residential trips, excursions and activities within the local community enhance our pupils’ educational experience and help them to develop their confidence and independence. Each school also runs an extensive range of after-school clubs each term, ranging from Robotics Club to Art Club, from Science Club to Athletics Club.
We believe that our approach ensures that our children’s outlook and horizons develop beyond their everyday experience.
We believe our approach ensures that our children’s outlook and horizons develop beyond their everyday experience.
The NMS Teaching and Learning Committee oversees the curriculum. To find out more about its work, click here.

All about Maple Walk
Welcome
Welcome to Maple Walk from our headteacher, Mia Santa-Humfrey
Welcome to Maple Walk. We are a forward-thinking prep school in North West London, close to Roundwood Park. We are a school with great heart, children are at the centre of everything we do, and every pupil is embraced as part of our shared community.
Our Story
Maple Walk was founded by the New Model School Company in 2004 with the simple philanthropic aim: to provide an excellent, affordable, prep education.
Vision and Values
A New Model School offers a great value education. We are forward thinking, sustainability is central to our ethos and our school buildings are modern and innovative. We deliver an ambitious knowledge-based curriculum that is taught in a creative way. We are confident that what we teach, is truly excellent.
Staff
Maple Walk has professional, enthusiastic staff all committed to instilling a love of lifelong learning in our pupils. Our teachers are academically ambitious for their students but care equally about wellbeing and creating an environment in which every child thrives.
Friends
The Friends of Maple Walk is a very active parent organisation and a vital part of the school community. All parents are encouraged to take part and their involvement strengthens the family feel of Maple Walk
Inspection Reports
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) Inspection Reports are the industry’s benchmark on the safety and quality of educational provision for schools in the private sector.
Directors and Advisors
We have a dedicated and highly experienced Board of Advisors and Directors who work closely with our school and support our growth.
Vacancies
We are always delighted to hear from teachers and support staff keen to join Maple Walk. We believe in doing schools differently and know that an excellent education starts with excellent people.
Policies
The school has comprehensive policies available to parents and prospective parents.

Meet our Head, Mia Santa-Humfrey
Welcome to
Maple Walk School
A small school with a big heart
Tucked away between the quiet residential streets of North West London, Maple Walk is a hidden gem: a vibrant, nurturing school community where every child is known, valued, and inspired to grow.
We believe the formative years are vital. They shape not only what children know, but who they become. At Maple Walk, we do more than just teach. We stretch without stress and encourage every child to discover their voice, their passions, and their path.
Our values, curiosity, creativity and community, underpin everything we do. We foster curious minds through a rich and imaginative curriculum, encourage creative expression in all its forms, and build a strong sense of belonging through shared experiences and close relationships.
Our small size is our strength. It allows us to tailor our teaching to each individual, offering high-quality instruction alongside exceptional pastoral care. Every child is seen, heard and supported, not just to succeed academically, but to flourish emotionally and socially.
We are proudly non-selective at entry, with no daunting assessments for those joining us in Reception. Yet by the time they leave us, our pupils are achieving places, often with academic, sporting or creative scholarships, at many of London’s top secondary schools (11+results). We help every child find their niche and grow in confidence, ready to take on the world.
Wellbeing is central to our approach. With smaller class sizes, daily mindfulness sessions, lunchtime wellbeing drop-ins, and dedicated lessons in positive psychology, we support each child’s emotional development. These foundations of wellbeing are not an add-on to learning; they are the groundwork that allows it to take place. By nurturing the whole child, we create the conditions where curiosity, creativity and academic potential can truly thrive.
Pupil voice is a key part of life at Maple Walk. From our empowered School Council to Year 6 pupils planning and delivering assemblies, children know their voices are heard and their contributions matter. Many take on additional leadership roles as Junior Travel Ambassadors or members of the Eco Committee, promoting sustainability and shared responsibility. Independence is further developed through participation in the Junior Duke programme, where children are encouraged to build practical life skills and confidence beyond the classroom.
Our commitment to the wider world is reflected in our eco-conscious ethos. The natural environment plays an integral role in school life. Roundwood Park, just on our doorstep, becomes an outdoor classroom for Forest School and sports, as well as a meeting place for early-morning athletics clubs and our environmentally-friendly ‘walking bus’.
At Maple Walk, children don’t just gain knowledge. They gain self-belief, empathy, independence, and a strong sense of who they are.
The very best way to understand what makes Maple Walk so special is to spend time with our pupils. They are the truest reflection of our school values and the heart of who we are.
Please contact us via our Admissions or Open Days pages to arrange a visit, or contact our Registrar, Stefanie Harvey, on admissions@maplewalkschool.co.uk or 020 8965 7374.
We so look forward to welcoming you.
Mia Santa-Humfrey Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Directors and Advisors - Maple Walk School
pageCache.text:
Directors and Advisors
We have a dedicated and highly experienced Board of Advisors and Directors who work closely with our school and support our growth.
John Ashmore MA (Edinburgh) French, has worked in a variety of industry sectors including yoghurts, toys, pet nutrition and premium spirits, where he has held positions in Marketing, Sales and General Management. Currently, he is Marketing Director Europe, Middle-East for Clearwater Seafoods, North America’s largest vertically integrated wild shellfish producer. John is a member of the Fishmongers’ Livery Company.
Alexandra Cornforth, MA (Oxon), M.Litt, rejoined the board on the 1st September and has held several Board and Trustee positions over the course of a thirty-five year career in financial services. She is currently Head of Corporate Governance for a FTSE 250 listed investment trust and is also a non executive director of an investment management company providing ethical investment solutions for charities and individuals.
Rajinder Funnell: BA, English Literature pursued a career in publishing with Hodder and Stoughton from 2001, later became a qualified early years practitioner and is a Montessori teacher, training at the Maria Montessori Institute in London. Since 2014, Rajinder has also been actively fundraising for the Rugby Portobello Trust (RPT) and, in 2022, became a Co- chair for one of their fundraising committees. The RPT is a children’s, youth and family support group, supporting the local community for over 135 years, and helping the youngest members build confidence, expand their horizons and realise their potential.
Deborah Livsey: LLB Hons (Exeter), CEO has had a 15 year career in finance which has taken her from London, to Hong Kong and Japan. She has been a governor responsible for safeguarding at Amesbury, a preparatory school in Hampshire since 2012 and a trustee of Send Family Link, a charity which supports children with a female family member in prison. She joined NMS in 2018 as its Chief Operating Officer and became CEO in July 2020.
Xavier Villers: MA (Oxon.), MSt, ACII (Chairman) Xavier spent his working career in the insurance industry in the City of London, specialising in the marine sector and extreme risks, as well as managing and integrating a number of different businesses. He now holds various non-executive roles in finance, charity, and education. He is a non-executive director of a multi academy trust which runs five primary schools over eight different sites in South London. He also resumed his own education, and recently completed a master‘s degree in historical studies focusing on 17th century English history.
Joanna Copland BA (Hons) QTS, PG Cert Dys, Mont Dip has worked in the independent sector for more than 30 years. Starting as an early years teacher, she was then Deputy Head of Thomas’s School, Clapham for 14 years before becoming Vice Principal of the Thomas’s Schools group, collaborating with the senior leaders and sharing best practice across the schools. Most recently she has been Head of Pre-Prep at Fulham School. Joanna is a member of the Educators’ Livery company and a judge for the Queen’s Commonwealth Essay competition.
Jonathan Cubitt: BA ACA is Bursar of Queen’s Gate School. Previous roles include Business Development Director of Charity HR and Finance Director of The Art Fund, the national art charity. Prior to that, he spent 15 years in accountancy, working for several leading accountancy firms.
Vania Georgeson, BA (Hons), MA, PGCE Vania is a former head teacher with a background in English and Drama, teaching in both state and independent schools. Under her 14 year headship, The Roche School in SW London became known for academic excellence, strong pastoral care, and a progressive approach to Equality, Diversity & Inclusion. She holds an MA from King’s College London/The Globe Theatre and has directed youth Shakespeare productions, and co-edited The Women Writers Handbook. Vania now runs speech classes for children and advises on parents on school placement and educational choices.
Jane Ritchie: Early Years Professional (CWDC), Cert Ed in Early Childhood Education over 40 years of experience working in Early Years Education. Jane has worked within the independent sector in advisory/management roles to nursery groups, schools, companies and individuals both in the UK and abroad. Her experience includes 9 years at the Alpha Plus Group as Director of Nurseries and Head of Early Years and owner of The Minors Nursery School, London from 1990 to August 2005.
Justin Shaw: MA (Cantab) is a former Director and Deputy Chairman of NMS, and was the company’s Chairman from its foundation in 2004 until 2008. He was also Chairman of Civitas and remains a trustee of the independent social policy think-tank. After receiving a Senior Exhibition in Philosophy at Cambridge, he studied law and was called to the Bar at Lincoln’s Inn. Justin is now a full-time writer. Recent novels include The Illumination of Merton Browne and Ten Weeks in Africa.
Natalie Smith: (Parent Advisor) LLB Hons (London School of Economics) LLM (Queen Mary University). Natalie is a parent of a child at Faraday Prep school and is also a member of the Friends of Faraday ( the School’s parent organisation). Natalie’s professional background is in law. She is a solicitor with extensive experience in both private practice and the civil service, specialising in criminal law and the criminal justice system.
Nisha Vidani: Nisha is a parent of 2 children at Maple Walk and is a successful CFO and Co-Owner of a medium sized business that exports and wholesales British and European FMCG. Nisha is a multi-award winning business executive having been awarded the Queen’s Award for Enterprise in International Trade on five occasions and featured in both the Sunday Times Fast Track 100 and International Track 200 as well as reported in JM Morgan’s Top 200 Female- Powered Businesses in both 2022 and 2023.
The Teaching and Learning Committee is the dynamo at the heart of Maple Walk. Its members are education specialists who oversee and drive our ambitious, knowledge-based curriculum.

ISI Inspection Reports
ISI Inspection, May 2024 Overview
We are delighted that Maple Walk’s excellent teaching and learning has been recognised in our recent Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) report; it is a testament to the dedication of our staff and their commitment to achieving consistently high standards. Read the full inspection report here
The inspectors commend the staff’s work across all areas including teaching, pupil well-being and our school community, highlighting that: ‘staff actively promote the wellbeing of pupils’ while ‘pupils are well known by the staff and supported in all aspects of their school lives’ and ‘teaching is well planned, and resources are used effectively to support pupils’ learning’.
The impact of our work can also be seen in recognition of pupils’ development, with inspectors noting that ‘pupils feel valued as individuals, and they understand the school’s values to be curious, creative and positive members of society’ and ‘pupils develop a secure sense of self and are respectful towards others’.
‘Pupils feel valued as individuals’ and ‘consistently demonstrate high levels of self-knowledge, self-esteem and self confidence.’
‘Leaders have developed a clear vision for the school which focuses on curiosity, creativity and community and they help to shape the teaching and learning environment as well as the pastoral care of the pupils.’
‘Pupils understand how they can contribute positively to the lives of those living and working in the locality and wider society.’
‘Pupils feel well prepared for transition to their senior school as a result of activities carefully designed by leaders to support them.’
‘Pupils speak about their work with confidence and are well supported in their learning by teachers who understand how best to help them.’
Under the new inspection framework, schools no longer receive a one-word judgement; instead, reports determine whether each section of the inspection was ‘met’ or ‘unmet’. We are delighted that Maple Walk was found to meet all 5 sections of the standards following the inspectorate’s visit in February 2025. Read the February 2025 inspection report here

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama and Dance - Maple Walk School
pageCache.text:
Drama and Dance
Drama is timetabled for each year group once a week with a specialist teacher. Drama is exciting, fun and hugely rewarding. It builds individual confidence and requires a high degree of personal discipline as well as developing collaboration and teamwork skills. Children also have a specialist dance lesson once a week up until Year Four.
Performing in front of an audience is an experience that can prove invaluable. Annual poetry and public speaking competitions help the children to gain confidence when on stage, as well as enriching their understanding of literature.
We have dance lessons for all children and they are encouraged to dance each week. We love dance at Maple Walk, finding any opportunity, including in local and national competitions. We even held our very own carnival in Roundwood Park, showing off our costume making, dancing and singing skills!
Dance and drama tuition is provided by a qualified LAMDA teacher, who helps children gain excellent grades in the annual examinations.
The after-school dance club has competed at the National Dance Challenge three years in a row and has reached the finals twice.

Music
There are many opportunities for music-making at school. From Reception, Music is a timetabled subject taught by a specialist teacher. The curriculum includes activities that illustrate important musical concepts and terms and introduces the children to significant composers and works.
In addition to whole class music lessons, pupils may choose to learn a variety of instruments taught by experienced peripatetic teachers, who are all professional musicians. These instruments include singing, flute, clarinet, piano, drums and guitar.
Great importance is placed on the enjoyment and appreciation of a variety of music, and children are encouraged to join the school choir and musical clubs such as Music Technology. Musical aptitude is studied in Year 5 and children who wish to take examinations are encouraged to do so.
Children, teachers and parents enjoy the musical performances that take place at school during the year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art and Design - Maple Walk School
pageCache.text:
Art and Design
Creativity in all its forms is central to the ethos of Maple Walk. Children learn to appreciate and value images and artefacts across times and cultures and learn to understand the contexts in which they were made.
In Art and Design, pupils reflect critically on their own and others’ work, judging quality and meaning. They learn to think and act as artists, craftspeople and designers, working creatively and intelligently. They develop an appreciation of art, craft and design, and their role in the creative and cultural industries that enrich their lives.
My three children have had a wonderful time at Maple Walk. As well as great learning environment, there’s a strong focus on the creative and musical arts, which my boys loved.
-Paul, Year 3 Parent
Creativity is entrenched at Maple Walk
We aim to encourage the development of imagination, original thought and personal expression.
For exceptionally talented artists, we offer a portfolio club to help pupils prepare for art scholarships. Our pupils are regularly offered art scholarships for senior school.

English
Reading is the gateway to knowledge. Once a child can read fluently and independently, they widen their world. We therefore place great emphasis on teaching children to read as early as possible in their school careers and encourage it as a hobby and a tool throughout their time with us.
Fiction, plays and poems form an integral part of many lessons, with not only the reading and comprehension of a text being significant, but also how theme, style, structure and language are used. Whole class, small group and independent reading activities enhance speaking, listening and writing tasks, develop reading skills and encourage personal enjoyment and enthusiasm for reading.
We teach reading by means of synthetic phonics, the traditional method of associating letters with sounds that has been proven to be the most effective way to teach children to read, including children with learning difficulties. Spelling, handwriting, vocabulary, grammatical accuracy and creative style are all developed to high standards. The children’s written work is regularly shared and celebrated in House meetings and assemblies.
We have many events in the school year that serve to promote literacy, including the much-coveted poetry competition, readathon and public speaking competition. We also invite authors to speak to the children and ensure there are workshops that show them how storytelling, writing and reading can be used to inspire others and make a difference.
Our aim is to have all children reading independently and feeling able to express themselves in writing by the end of Year 1.
To achieve this, we ask for the support of parents, who are encouraged to read to – and with – their children every day. Working in partnership with parents is very important to us and helps the children to progress rapidly.

Humanities
History
History provides valuable insights into the world we live in today. By understanding the past, our children can grasp how societies, cultures, and civilizations have evolved over time. This knowledge helps them make sense of current events and appreciate the significance of certain developments or issues.
At school, our history curriculum promotes critical thinking skills. Analysing historical events, causes, and consequences encourages pupils to examine evidence, evaluate different perspectives, and develop their own informed opinions.
By studying the experiences of different individuals and societies throughout history, children can develop an understanding of diverse perspectives and cultures. This fosters tolerance, respect, and an appreciation for the shared humanity of people from different backgrounds.
Areas covered by the curriculum include:
Geography
Geography gives us a sense of place in the world.
As children become familiar with globes, maps and atlases, they appreciate both their local environment as well as their relation to the country and continent they inhabit, and the world beyond. Geography helps us to understand why settlements grew up where they did, how the world’s resources are accessed and transported, and what processes shape the world around us. Our approach emphasises human as well as physical geography and the study of the cultures, languages, arts and industries of the many and varied places on Earth.
Religious Education
Religious Education aims to enable pupils to develop an understanding of other cultures and lifestyles.
Pupils have an opportunity to explore stories and beliefs from a variety of religions, including Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism and Sikhism. Pupils also study Philosophy and ask ‘big’ questions in their weekly Mindful Mouse discussions.
The curriculum is delivered creatively by teachers using drama, discussions, debates, visits to places of worship and sessions with outside speakers.

Science
We see Science as an essential discipline for young children. Our curriculum will lay the foundation for pupils to understand what the discipline of Science tells us about the world. We aim to ignite children’s love for science by showing them what fascinating things the human race has learned about the world.
Science teaches an understanding of natural phenomena. We aim to stimulate a child’s curiosity in finding out why things happen in the way they do. It teaches methods of enquiry and investigation to stimulate creative thought. Children learn to ask scientific questions and begin to appreciate the way that Science will affect their future on a personal, national and global level.
We go beyond the national curriculum in what we teach.
Children are introduced to topics including the inner workings of the human body, animals and the environments they live in, plants and their features, forces of nature, and what lies beyond the visible world. Children are taught to apply their knowledge and conduct their own scientific enquiries to answer questions, working scientifically to develop essential skills. Every opportunity is taken to allow the children to experience the practical aspects of the subject.
Our science curriculum builds knowledge incrementally year-on-year to revisit and build upon children’s knowledge and understanding of key concepts. Pupils also study the lives and achievements of a diverse range of scientists including Lewis Howard Latimer, Thomas Edison, Jabir ibn Hayyan. Their disciplinary knowledge will flourish over time, enabling them to see the importance of science as a subject, how it translates into the world of research and work, what scientists do and how they impact upon our lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wellbeing and PSHE - Maple Walk School
pageCache.text:
Wellbeing and PSHE
PSHE teaches children the skills they need to make appropriate decisions about their lives now and in the future. It also encourages children to develop confidence and a sense of responsibility. Pupils are encouraged to develop good relationships with peers and staff, as well as a healthy understanding of the many differences between people.
PSHE is taught as a stand-alone subject and also through other curriculum subjects, assemblies and class discussions. It is an integral part of every school day.
Emphasis is placed on active learning through discussion, investigation and problem-solving activities. Children are rewarded for positive behaviour by members of staff in a range of ways, including earning House points, extra play, stickers and certificates.
Children experience democracy through our School Council which is made up of elected representatives from Year 2 upwards.
Relationships and Sex Education is taught as part of our curriculum, in line with national guidance. Our curriculum is delivered through lessons by the Family Planning Association, samples of which can be found here. Curriculum maps and learning outcomes can be found in the appendix of our RSE policy, which is available in the ‘Policies and Key Information’ section of the website. Lesson plans and resources can be made available in full upon request to the school office.
In response to feedback from our parent consultation in July 2026, please find further guidance from the NSPCC to support talking to children about difficult topics as well as a recommended reading list.

Friends of Maple Walk
The Friends of Maple Walk is a very active parent organisation and a vital part of the school community. All parents are encouraged to take part. Their involvement strengthens the family feel of Maple Walk.
“We love the school due to its small, friendly, welcoming feel. Our daughter has been extremely happy throughout her school journey. The parent network is also close and extremely supportive.”
-Simone, Year 5 Parent
During a typical year, the Friends raise money through a Christmas Fair, stalls at local community fairs, a huge social event which includes an auction, quiz nights, a large range of Christmas merchandise designed by the children, as well as many other social events. The money has been used to provide a huge range of things for the school such as staging, play equipment, musical equipment, a sound system, beet-box cameras, laptops, books, bikes, scooters and gymnastic equipment. Thanks to their support the school opened the Secret Garden, an outdoor learning space designed by parents and children.
Other events organised by the Friends include Book Week and Art Week extravaganzas, workshops, outside speakers, additional sports activities gardening and painting teams. These are enriching opportunities for parents and children alike that greatly enhance the school community.

Wellbeing
The wellbeing of our children is at the heart of all we do.
Care for our pupils is embedded in our school culture.
We take time to get to know our children.
Wellbeing is a central focus of life at Maple Walk and one of our greatest strengths is our wonderful staff team who consistently go above and beyond for the children in their care. Children learn best when they feel safe, encouraged and that they truly belong. All staff know all children well, ensuring everyone feels seen and valued.
We offer a dedicated Wellbeing Zone where children can enjoy quiet time during their lunch break alongside a range of activities that change daily. On Wednesdays, our ‘Talk Time’ space allows children to sign up in advance to speak with an experienced member of staff about any worries or big feelings.
During ‘Seeds of Happiness’ lessons, delivered by the headteacher, children learn about the science of happiness and how their brains work. These sessions help children to understand emotions, build resilience and develop positive strategies for wellbeing. By exploring how thoughts, feelings and behaviours are connected, pupils are supported to grow in confidence, self-awareness and emotional literacy, equipping them with skills they can use both in and out of school.
Our wellbeing provision is further enhanced by our dedicated school therapy dog, Nova, who visits Maple Walk every Monday and Thursday. Nova is currently training through the PAWS Therapy Dogs Programme and plays a valuable role in supporting children’s emotional wellbeing. As well as spending time in the Wellbeing Zone each Monday for calm strokes and cuddles, Nova works with individuals and small groups to support regulation, confidence and engagement, both in the classroom and beyond.
Pastoral care is to the fore and emotional issues tend to be picked up early
-A Maple Walk parent speaking to the Good Schools Guide

pageCache.pageTitle: NMS Foundation Maple Walk Award 2026 - Maple Walk School
pageCache.text:
NMS Foundation Maple Walk Award 2026
The NMS Foundation Maple Walk Award provides a fully funded or subsidised place for a child joining Maple Walk School in Year 3.
The award will cover up to 100% of the school fees for a child who would otherwise be unable to attend and is currently attending a state school in Year 2.
Selection is based on the candidate’s current school report, a taster day at the school, which includes some assessments (no advance preparation is needed), and a school reference. Short-listed candidates are invited back with their parent(s) for an interview.
We look for candidates whose parents would not otherwise be able to afford an independent education and who would benefit from Maple Walk’s offer.
Applications for September 2026 are now closed.
The New Model School company was started over twenty years ago with the aim of offering excellent affordable education, with the launch of the New Model School Foundation last year, The NMS Foundation Maple Walk Award will give an opportunity for a child to join Maple Walk with a fully funded place. This continues the original vision of the New Model School Company to broaden the reach of an excellent education to as many children as possible.
Please contact the Admissions Registrar, Stefanie Harvey, on 020 8965 7374 or by email at stefanie.harvey@newmodelschool.co.uk if you have any questions about the award.
For more information about The New Model School Foundation please visit link to the NMSF page on the NMS Website
